sections.heading: The Slow-Lift Opening Money Can Hear
sections.text: Ultra-Premium Construction The Slow-Lift Opening Money Can Hear A shoulder-neck box is engineered theatre. The inner neck (the 'shoulder') stands proud of the base, so the lid floats on a visible reveal gap — often in a contrast colour — and lifts against an air cushion with a controlled, audible glide. It's the construction behind most flagship perfume and cognac presentations. The three-piece build demands tolerance control: lid-to-neck clearance is held at 0.3–0.5mm so the glide is smooth but never loose. Contrast neck colours, foil bands on the gap line, and interior platforms for bottles or jewels complete the format. Compare the simpler two-piece lid & base , or see it applied on the perfume packaging page .

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text: Questions Frequently Asked Questions What exactly is a shoulder-neck box? A three-piece rigid construction: the base carries a proud inner neck, and the lid floats on that neck leaving a visible reveal gap — giving the slow, cushioned lift used by flagship perfume and spirits brands. Why does the lid lift so slowly? Lid-to-neck clearance is held at 0.3–0.5mm, trapping an air cushion; the glide is tuned and tested on every prototype. Can the neck be a contrast colour? Yes — contrast wraps and foil band lines on the reveal gap are the signature styling options of this format. Is it suitable for heavy bottles? Yes, with 2.5mm board and platform mounts we run 340mm spirits formats; weight is declared and tested at prototype. What is the MOQ? 200 pcs; tolerance-tuned prototypes in 5–7 business days.
